T-box riboreulators are a new class of riboregulators that are able to decode and read the aminoacylation states of specific tRNAs to regulate the expression of their cognate aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (ARS) genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T-box consists not of two but three domains: the decoding domain (Stem-I and Stem-II), the antitermination domain (Stem-III), and the aminoacylation-sensing domain (linker).
T-boxes have evolved to use a claw-like decoding and an antiterminator-based aminoacylation sensing mechanism to achieve their regulatory function.
a single riboregulator can use two different sets of interactions to recognize and respond to two different states of the same tRNA.
